*   Linting an Astro file with experimentalFullSupportEnabled and the useImportType rule must produce the output 'No fixes applied' when all component imports are correctly used as rendered elements in the template section.

## Summary

I fixed the `useImportType` rule so it no longer suggests converting a component import to a type-only import when that component is used as a JSX/rendered element in an Astro file's template section.

### Root cause

Astro template component usages were being missed in two paths:

1. **Full HTML support enabled** — Astro `{…}` template expressions are parsed as TSX, so `<Card />` becomes a `JsxReferenceIdentifier`. The value-reference tracker (`visit_non_source_snippet`) only recognized `JsReferenceIdentifier` / `JsStaticMemberExpression`, so JSX element names were never counted as value uses.
2. **Full HTML support disabled** (default Astro handler) — the file is parsed as JS frontmatter only, so the template markup (e.g. top-level `<Component />`) was never parsed at all, leaving no value references for it.

In both cases, if the same import was also referenced in a type position (e.g. `Array<typeof Component>`) in the frontmatter, the rule wrongly flagged it.

### Changes (source only)

- **`crates/biome_service/src/workspace/document/services/embedded_value_references.rs`**: `visit_non_source_snippet` now also tracks `JsxReferenceIdentifier` nodes as value references (`<Card />` tracks `Card`; `<Layout.Slot />` tracks the base `Layout`). Added a unit test.
- **`crates/biome_service/src/workspace/server.rs`**: Added `track_astro_template_components`, invoked in both `open_file`/`change_file` value-reference builders. When an Astro file isn't handled by the HTML component path (i.e. full support is off), it parses the raw content as an Astro template and records template component names as value references.
- **`.changeset/astro-use-import-type-jsx-components.md`**: changeset describing the fix.

### Verification

- New behavior confirmed against reproductions for all four requirements (default and full-support modes), including named/default imports and `typeof` in generic type arguments → all report `No fixes applied`.
- Negative case preserved: an import used only as a type and *not* in the template is still correctly flagged.
- All existing tests pass: `biome_service` unit tests (5), `handle_astro_files` (30), `handle_vue_files` (45), `handle_svelte_files` (25).

One deliberate non-goal: JSX inside `{…}` expressions in *non-full-support* mode is still not tracked, because that path never parses the inner template JavaScript — this isn't implied by the requirements (the full-support case covers JSX-in-expressions; the default case covers top-level components).

I did not modify anything under `tests/` directories.
